subject: Nanotechnology
title: Lab on a Chip
description: Learn Lab on a Chip in one minute.

hook.text: An entire blood test lab shrunk to a chip the size of a credit card — that is a lab on a chip.

buildup.text: Microfluidic channels guide tiny sample volumes through mixing, separation, and detection — all on one device.

discovery.text: Nano-structured sensors inside the channels detect biomarkers at concentrations invisible to standard tests.

twist.text: Manufacturing reproducible nano-features inside channels at scale is still challenging — yield varies widely.

climax.text: Abbott's i-STAT handheld analyzer runs blood tests in two minutes at the patient's bedside — lab-on-chip is real.

punchline.text: Shrink the lab onto a chip and diagnostics go anywhere.

quiz.question: What is the key advantage of lab-on-a-chip diagnostics?
options: They can test larger sample volumes than traditional labs
They miniaturize testing onto a portable chip for rapid point-of-care results
They eliminate the need for any reagents
